findings.title: website_name bypasses anonymous TL0 website hiding
findings.body: website_name is computed from the profile website, but it is not subject to the same anonymous trust-level-0 restriction as website. untrusted_attributes only defines include_<attr>? for bio, location, website, and the background fields, and that guard is what stops anonymous viewers (and crawlers hitting /users/:username.json) from seeing a new user's website. The new include_website_name method is never called: this serializer, like ActiveModel Serializers 0.8, only invokes include_website_name? (question mark), which is how every other include hook in this file is named. Even if it were renamed, it only returns website.present? and never calls scope.restrict_user_fields?(object). Previously the client derived the label from model.website, so when website was omitted the globe link disappeared. Now an anonymous profile request for a TL0 user omits website but still receives website_name (host, and host+path when the comparison matches), and the template renders it. That restores the spam-visible website the restriction exists to hide. Put :website_name in untrusted_attributes and delete this include method; a later include_website_name? that only checks website.present? would override the macro and keep the leak. As written, users with a blank website also always get "website_name": null, because the include hook does not run.

findings.title: Same-domain check mis-classifies hosts
findings.body: website_name's host comparison does not match "same domain", so the path is added for unrelated sites and omitted for equivalent ones. Equality and ends_with? are case-sensitive, but Ruby's URI parser keeps host case and Discourse.current_hostname is lowercase: http://Example.com/user on a forum at example.com fails every branch and displays Example.com with no path. The sibling branch (same label count > 2, then compare everything after the first label) treats evil.co.uk and forum.co.uk, or a.github.io and b.github.io, as the same site because the shared suffix is a public suffix, and appends the path. The else branch's discourse_host.ends_with?("." + website_host) is true for any suffix, so a website host of com matches every *.com forum and the label becomes com plus the path. The parent check is one-way: example.com on a www.example.com forum includes the path, but http://www.example.com/user on an example.com forum does not, because the label counts differ and example.com does not end with .www.example.com. Profile labels will therefore show paths for unrelated domains and hide paths for the same site entered with different case or a www prefix.

findings.title: Displayed website name drops non-default ports
findings.body: website_name keeps only URI#host, which never includes the port, then optionally appends the path. The removed client label used website.split("/")[2], so http://example.com:8443/app was shown as example.com:8443. It is now shown as example.com when the host is unrelated, or example.com/app when the host comparison matches. The href is still the original URL, but the visible text identifies the default port. Any profile website on a non-default port is mislabeled, including links that are not on the forum domain.

findings.title: Specs miss the TL0 leak and domain edge cases
findings.body: The anonymous TL0 example still only asserts that bio, location, website, and background keys are absent, and it never sets a website. website_name is therefore free to appear in that JSON (as a host/path, or as null when the include hook does not run) without failing the suite. The new examples only stub current_hostname to discourse.org, example.com, and forums.example.com against an already-lowercased http://example.com/user, so they do not catch case-sensitive misses, port stripping, the www child case, or false matches such as another *.co.uk host or a website host of com. Those are the paths that produce the wrong label or the privacy leak, and the added specs still pass if they ship.
